title: Programmatic Representation Learning with Language Models

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-synthesized programmatic features for supervised prediction
mechanism.populationDetail: No population of competing candidate solutions is maintained; the accumulated feature set is part of a supervised predictor.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No elite solution archive is described.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Replacement taxonomy is not applicable: F2 appends generated features to predictor inputs, not evolutionary individuals; D-ID3 tree nodes are predictive splits, not a search population.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM proposes new feature functions as code; prior features, scores, paths, or examples are conditioning context, not editable parent candidates.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: F2 feeds Random Forest feature-importance scores back into later proposal prompts. D-ID3 uses split-error/impurity scores to select the split, without reported natural-language evaluator feedback.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No editable parent solution is selected. Context features, examples, and decision-tree paths are not evolutionary parents.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: LLM-generated feature-function synthesis integrated into supervised representation learning, including global feature-importance feedback (F2) and local error-conditioned feature synthesis (D-ID3), is outside evolutionary-search population and parent mechanisms.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/PROGRAMMATIC REPRESENTATION LEARNING WITH LANGUAGE MODELS.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: This paper is not an LLM evolutionary-search system. Chapter 4 placements are cautious analogical mappings for candidate-generation prompts and from-scratch code generation; population, archives, replacement, multi-model routing, and parent selection should not be inferred from the feature set or predictive decision tree.
